paper_title: Attributing Response to Context A Jensen-Shannon Divergence Driven   Mechanistic Study of Context Attribution in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
caption: Computational efficiency comparison between our ARC-JSD and Contextcite (n=256 calls) across all datasets and RAG models. Each bar represents the average seconds per sample for ARC-JSD and Contextcite with different RAG models and datasets.
model_annotation: The bar chart titled “Computational Efficiency: ARC-JSD vs. Contextcite” presents a comparison of average computational time per sample, measured in seconds, between two methods—ARC-JSD and Contextcite—across four large language models (Qwen2-1.5B-IT, Qwen2-7B-IT, Gemma2-2B-IT, Gemma2-9B-IT) and three datasets (TyDi QA, Hotpot QA, MuSiQue). The horizontal axis lists the models in ascending order of parameter size, while the vertical axis represents “Seconds/Sample,” scaled linearly from 0 to 80 with major gridlines at intervals of 20. For each model, six grouped bars are displayed, corresponding to the six combinations of method and dataset as defined in the legend: ARC-JSD - TyDi QA (dark blue), Contextcite - TyDi QA (orange), ARC-JSD - Hotpot QA (medium blue), Contextcite - Hotpot QA (light orange), ARC-JSD - MuSiQue (light blue), and Contextcite - MuSiQue (pale orange). Across all models and datasets, Contextcite consistently exhibits higher computational cost than ARC-JSD, with the disparity increasing for larger models and more complex datasets; for instance, on Gemma2-9B-IT with MuSiQue, Contextcite reaches approximately 85 seconds/sample, while ARC-JSD is around 31 seconds/sample. The bars for each model are arranged in a fixed order per dataset pair, and no bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or annotations beyond their color-coded representation in the legend.
